intro.title: Lesson focus
intro.body: Class 1 / Numbers and Counting / Counting and Number Sense Counting objects to 20 is a number-sense lesson in Counting and Number Sense. It helps children connect spoken numbers, written numerals, quantities, and place value. This lesson uses a clear model, a worked example, and a short practice task suited to counting objects to 20.

learn.title: Explanation
learn.body: Counting objects to 20: Use objects, ten-frames, bundles, or place-value charts so each number has a visible meaning.
bullets: Show the quantity with objects or a place-value chart.
Say the number aloud and write the numeral.
For counting objects to 20, group tens and ones when helpful.
Check: check by recounting or comparing with a nearby number.

learn.title: Common mistake
learn.body: In counting objects to 20, show why 'Show the quantity with objects or a place-value chart.' is valid before using the method.

intro.title: Lesson focus
intro.body: Class 2 / Measurement / Metric Awareness Comparing measurements is a measurement lesson in Metric Awareness. It uses numbers and units to compare length, mass, capacity, time, money, area, or volume. This lesson uses a clear model, a worked example, and a short practice task suited to comparing measurements.

learn.title: Explanation
learn.body: Comparing measurements: Choose the correct unit first, then measure, convert, or calculate with units visible.
bullets: Identify what is being measured.
Choose a sensible unit.
For comparing measurements, measure or calculate.
Check: write the answer with the unit and check reasonableness.

learn.title: Common mistake
learn.body: In comparing measurements, a number without a unit is incomplete.

examples.title: Worked example
examples.body: A pencil may be 14 cm long; a water bottle may hold 1 litre; a book may weigh 300 g.
